text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A states a clear position against driverless cars and organizes three distinct reasons, each developed in its own body paragraph with a conclusion restating the position.", "quality": "Clear argumentative structure", "description": "The essay presents a clear thesis and develops each supporting reason in a separate paragraph with an introduction, body, and conclusion."}, {"evidence": "Essay A quotes the article directly (e.g., \"Google cars aren't truly driverless...\" and \"If the technology fails and someone is injured, who is at fault...\") and ties each quote to its argument.", "quality": "Effective use of textual evidence", "description": "The essay integrates direct quotations from the source and connects each one to the specific claim it supports."}, {"evidence": "Essay A reasons about why the 25 mph limit, the need for driver alertness, and liability concerns undermine the value of driverless cars, offering its own interpretation of the quoted material.", "quality": "Analytical reasoning", "description": "The essay goes beyond restating the article to explain why each cited detail weakens the case for driverless cars."}, {"evidence": "Essay A maintains a consistent first-person argumentative voice throughout, while Essay B mostly summarizes and narrates the article's content without taking a clear stance.", "quality": "Sustained argumentative stance", "description": "The essay consistently argues its own position rather than merely retelling or summarizing the source article."}, {"evidence": "Essay A uses topic sentences like \"My first reason I wouldnt want this car is...\" and \"My second reason why i would not want a driverless car is...\" to signal each new point.", "quality": "Coherent paragraph organization", "description": "Each paragraph is anchored by a clear topic sentence that previews the point being argued."}]}
